cuts.item: Pavement management restoration to 650,000 (town manager's budget shows 279,000)
Recycling program budget reduced to estimated 350,000 from larger budget last year
Traffic signs line painting line reduced
Conservation administrative assistant eliminated effective July 1
Communications and IT director position eliminated
Treasurer expense lines reduced from preliminary budget
Collector budget reduction, mainly contracted services
Town accountant budget reduction since preliminary
Liability insurance reduced slightly; ClearGov premium eliminated
Special assistant to the assessor moved out of operating budget to one-time sources
IT salary line reduced to zero

statements.statement: Free cash was certified this week for the general fund.
DPW budget request is 3.178 million, higher than previous years; includes part-time clerk, MS4 compliance money, and restored pavement management.
DPW request restores pavement management to 650,000; the town manager's budget shows only 279,000, and the town manager said she won't support the restoration in the final budget.
Storm water line increase of 340,000 for MS4 permit compliance (catch basin cleaning and sweeping).
Chapter 90 for FY27 is 718,000, versus a typical 415,000.
Sewer enterprise budget is just shy of $2 million, with a surplus of about $26,000 after a rate increase; no retained earnings used.
Sewer user rate increase of 16% proposed, to 1838 from 1585; without it the deficit would be almost $200,000.
Land use budget request of $447,963, a 1.77% increase.
Trust fund commissioners request a warrant article appropriating $14,252.39 for legal investigation of neglected trust funds; Finance Committee member recommended pushing to special town meeting.
Total deficit right now is $3,123,989, about 1.24 million town and 1.9 million school, with school at full budget restoration of 28,456,277.
School full budget restoration number.
Estimated property tax levy is 36,332,000 of total revenues 49,750 (thousand).
General government budget now $3,225,72125 versus preliminary $3,25,5124 (as captioned).
Town manager budget is $442,353, up 44.88%, including full-year assistant town manager.
Audit cost raised from $40,000 to $65,000.
Finance committee reserve fund level funded at 185,000; town manager would consider raising it.
Intergovernmental assessments, up $238,289.95 or 9.94%, nearly all Worcester County retirement.
General government unclassified (insurance) now $4,500,42459 versus preliminary $4,312,412, due to staff error.
Group health insurance total increase of $193,44027.
At the tri-board all agreed the warrant should contain an override; 7 favored one number and 6 favored two (core service and a higher one).

warnings.prediction: Elimination of the communications and IT director will diminish external communications and affect departmental websites, IT and graphic design.

warnings.condition: if the storm water line is not restored
warnings.prediction: Not restoring the storm water money risks EPA fines (probably not) and continued impaired water bodies.

warnings.condition: if pavement management line stays reduced
warnings.prediction: If pavement management is reduced, more Chapter 90 must go to paving and drainage projects drop out.
Unemployment line may need to be addressed if layoffs are anticipated.
Further reductions expected in other budgets as second pass tightens; budgets getting close to the margins.
Intergovernmental assessments growing about 10% a year could become unmanageable.
